proof:
# A compatible plateau can have no inverse-power-concave minorant of half its mass

This is an exact obstruction to a GEOMETRY-ONLY single-minorant strategy. It retains one integer coordinate, positive compatible full-dimensional fibers, a full-rank occupied homothetic source interval with an interior integer witness, and a global positive affine homothetic envelope. It does NOT assert that these source labels are actual deepest bases, that the family minimizes the H objective, or that it admits the required actual common-Q critical menu. Those additional constraints remain possible decisive inputs.

## 1. Actual convex family and pointed density

Set d=32, p=d+1=33, and let D be the closed Euclidean unit ball in R^d, with volume v_d. Define

    C={(z,x):0<=z<=4, ||x||<=min(z+1,3)}.

The radius is positive and concave on [0,4], so C is a full-dimensional compact convex body. Its complete integer base is {0,1,2,3,4}; its fiber radii are 1,2,3,3,3. Let ell(z)=z+1 and y(z)=0. Then

    C_z subset ell(z)D,
    C_z=ell(z)D for all real z in B=[0,2].

The interval B has the interior integer witness 1. The pointed sampled density is

    f(xi)=F_2 1_D(xi)+4^d 1_((3/4)D)(xi)
                         +5^d 1_((3/5)D)(xi),       (1)
    F_j=sum_(k=1)^(j+1) k^d, j=2,3,4.

Thus its total mass, equal to the original mixed volume, is

    M=v_d[1+2^d+3·3^d].                             (2)

We prove that every measurable g satisfying 0<=g<=f almost everywhere and whose extended inverse p-th root is convex has

    integral g <=(1165/999) v_d 3^d < M/2.           (3)

The zero density is trivial. Boundedness and compact support follow from g<=f. No numerical evidence is used.

## 2. Symmetric decreasing rearrangement preserves the relevant class

Write h=g^(-1/p) on {g>0}, extended by infinity elsewhere. For each finite level t the sublevel K_t={h<=t} is convex. Replace each K_t by the centered ball of the same volume. These balls are nested. Their radius R(t)=(|K_t|/v_d)^(1/d) is concave on the interval of positive-volume levels, because

    (1-a)K_s+a K_t subset K_((1-a)s+a t)

and ordinary Brunn--Minkowski gives the concavity inequality for R. Consequently the radial generalized inverse h_star(r) of R is convex and nondecreasing on its finite domain. Flat or empty initial sublevels are handled by the usual generalized inverse; equivalently its epigraph is the inverse of the hypograph of the nondecreasing concave radius R. The resulting density g_star=h_star^(-p) is the symmetric decreasing rearrangement of g and has the same integral.

Since f is radially nonincreasing, g<=f implies |{g>t}|<=|{f>t}| at every level t. Rearranging these superlevels gives g_star<=f almost everywhere. Thus it suffices to bound radial densities g(r)=h(r)^(-p), where h is positive, convex and nondecreasing on the interior of a ball support. Positivity follows from the finite upper bound F_4 on g. Convex h is continuous at every interior radius.

The proof only uses almost-everywhere inequalities, so representatives at the two jump spheres of f do not affect it.

## 3. A quasiconcave radial ratio allows at most one unpenalized shell

Put

    r_2=1, r_3=3/4, r_4=3/5,
    a=max{r_3 F_2^(1/p), r_4 F_3^(1/p)}.             (4)

For k(r)=r/h(r), every strict superlevel is an interval: {k>a} is {h(r)-r/a<0}, a convex sublevel in the one-dimensional radius variable. Extend k by zero outside the support of g.

If r_j, j=3,4, is strictly inside that support, then continuity of h and the upper bound g<=F_(j-1) immediately OUTSIDE the sphere r_j imply

    k(r_j)<=r_j F_(j-1)^(1/p)<=a.                   (5)

If the support ends at r_j, it cannot cross that radius, so the same separation conclusion holds without assuming continuity through a support endpoint. Hence the interval {k>a} lies in at most one of the three shells

    (r_3,1], (r_4,r_3], [0,r_4].

On that one shell, its g mass is at most its f mass, and consequently at most

    v_d max_(j=2,3,4) F_j r_j^d.                   (6)

This bound allows the last shell to include the center and allows the positive set {k>a} to be empty.

On the complement k<=a, both g<=F_4 and g<=a^p r^(-p) hold. Integrating this elementary majorant over ALL radii, with r_0=a F_4^(-1/p), gives

    integral_(k<=a) g
       <= d v_d integral_0^infinity
                       min(F_4,a^p r^(-p)) r^(d-1) dr
       = (d+1) v_d a^d F_4^(1/p).                  (7)

Indeed the integral below r_0 is v_d a^d F_4^(1/p), and the remaining integral is d times that quantity since p=d+1. Combining (6)--(7),

    integral g <=v_d max_j F_j r_j^d
                         +(d+1)v_d a^d F_4^(1/p). (8)

## 4. Exact numerical-free estimate

Let q=4/5. Adjacent terms in every sum F_j, j<=4, have ratio at most q^d. Thus

    F_j <= (j+1)^d/(1-q^d).

It follows that

    max_j F_j r_j^d <= 3^d/(1-q^d),
    a <=3q(1-q^d)^(-1/p),
    F_4^(1/p)<=5(1-q^d)^(-1/p).

Substitution into (8) yields

    integral g <=v_d 3^d [1+5(d+1)q^d]/(1-q^d).    (9)

For d=32,

    q^d=(4/5)^32<1/1000,

an exact integer inequality 1000·4^32<5^32. Therefore (9) implies

    integral g <v_d 3^d (1+165/1000)/(1-1/1000)
               =(1165/999)v_d 3^d.

Since 2·1165=2330<2997=3·999, this is strictly less than (3/2)v_d 3^d, which is at most M/2 by (2). This proves (3).

## 5. Scope

The obstruction defeats not just one natural scalar filling but EVERY dominated density in the exact inverse-(d+1)-power-concave class. It also defeats a density with convex inverse beta-th root for any beta>=d+1: its inverse (d+1)-st root is the convex increasing power h^(beta/(d+1)). Therefore affine-tilted fillings, positive-part shifted fillings, and their other modifications within the admissible radial class cannot supply half the original mass on this geometric family.

The example has actual fiber masses 1,2^d,3^d,3^d,3^d times v_d. No original fiber has mass M/2. Its designated source-interval mass is (1+2^d+3^d)v_d, also less than M/2 (since 1+2^d<3^d). Thus neither the original-heavy-fiber nor the whole-source-interval alternative removes the obstruction.

Its pointed density is radially symmetric, so it certainly does not refute OC; its ordinary pointed depth at zero is 1/2. The missing actual deepest/common-Q menu data cannot be silently supplied. A usable minorant proof must exploit those data, allow multiple densities with an additional verified cap-selection argument, or use a weaker numerical mechanism than a single half-mass inverse-power-concave minorant.
